candidates.title: LEMS: a language for expressing complex biological models in concise and hierarchical form and its use in underpinning NeuroML 2
candidates.authors: Robert C. Cannon, Padraig Gleeson, Sharon Crook, Gautham Ganapathy, Boris Marin, Eugenio Piasini, et al. (7 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: DOI in README of GitHub LEMS/LEMS and NeuroML/NeuroML2; verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Canonical citation for LEMS, the simulation/behaviour description language underlying NeuroML 2 that NeuroSem will parse, simulate and mutate. Reused infrastructure; no mutation, protocol battery or behavioural regression testing.

candidates.title: The NeuroML ecosystem for standardized multi-scale modeling in neuroscience
candidates.authors: Ankur Sinha, Padraig Gleeson, Bóris Marin, Salvador Dura-Bernal, Sotirios Panagiotou, Sharon Crook, et al. (11 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (NeuroML ecosystem); verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Current canonical citation for the NeuroML 2 ecosystem (schema, libNeuroML, pyNeuroML, jNeuroML, validation and simulation tooling). Crossref abstract lists validation and simulation among ecosystem functions. Reused infrastructure, not a behavioural-drift detection method.

candidates.title: libNeuroML and PyLEMS: using Python to combine procedural and declarative modeling approaches in computational neuroscience
candidates.authors: Michael Vella, Robert C. Cannon, Sharon Crook, Andrew P. Davison, Gautham Ganapathy, Hugh P. C. Robinson, et al. (8 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: DOI in README of GitHub NeuralEnsemble/libNeuroML; verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Canonical citation for libNeuroML and PyLEMS, the Python APIs NeuroSem would use to read/write and programmatically mutate NeuroML models. Infrastructure only.

candidates.title: NeuroML/pyNeuroML: v1.3.22
candidates.authors: Ankur Sinha, Padraig Gleeson, Aditya Pandey, Richard C Gerkin, Giannis Daras, Robert Vickerstaff (first creators per DataCite)
candidates.venue: Zenodo (software record; metadata via DataCite API)
candidates.found_via: GitHub org:NeuroML search + DOI badge in pyNeuroML README; DataCite API; PyPI JSON (pyneuroml 1.3.22)
candidates.why_relevant: pyNeuroML is the Python entry point for validating, simulating and translating NeuroML/LEMS models that NeuroSem plans to reuse. DataCite record: version v1.3.22, rights lgpl-3.0; PyPI JSON latest 1.3.22; GitHub license LGPL-3.0. Provides execution and validation, not mutation-calibrated perturbation testing.

candidates.title: NeuroML/jNeuroML (Java command line tool and library to validate, simulate, translate and analyse NeuroML 2 models)
candidates.authors: Padraig Gleeson, Ankur Sinha, Russell Jarvis, Finn Krewer (first creators per DataCite)
candidates.venue: GitHub; Zenodo release records (e.g. v0.14.0, DataCite year 2025)
candidates.found_via: GitHub org:NeuroML validation search; DataCite Zenodo query jNeuroML
candidates.why_relevant: Planned pilot simulator (handoff: jNeuroML only). GitHub description covers validation, simulation, translation to other simulators. Translation outputs are exactly the kind of transformation whose behaviour preservation NeuroSem would test. [GitHub API: created 2012-12-18, license LGPL-3.0; DataCite DOI 10.5281/zenodo.593108 titled NeuroML/jNeuroML: v0.14.0]

candidates.title: Open Source Brain: A Collaborative Resource for Visualizing, Analyzing, Simulating, and Developing Standardized Models of Neurons and Circuits
candidates.authors: Padraig Gleeson, Matteo Cantarelli, Boris Marin, Adrian Quintana, Matt Earnshaw, Sadra Sadeh, et al. (27 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: osb-model-validation README links the OSB paper; DOI resolved by Crossref bibliographic query and verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Canonical citation for Open Source Brain; per OMV README, OMV was used to test the 30+ NeuroML and PyNN models described in this paper. Continuous automated model testing across simulators is the closest community infrastructure to NeuroSem regression testing, but it checks fixed expected behaviours rather than mutation-calibrated multi-protocol fingerprints.

candidates.title: OSB Model Validation (OMV): tools for automated model validation in Open Source Brain projects
candidates.authors: OpenSourceBrain (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search osb-model-validation; PyPI JSON OSBModelValidation 0.4.0
candidates.why_relevant: OMV runs declarative tests (OMT/MEP files) of model behaviour on many simulation engines under CI, per its README. Directly overlaps NeuroSem on executable regression tests of NeuroML models and cross-simulator checks; no controlled mutants, protocol-battery optimisation, tolerance calibration by refinement, or held-out evaluation found in README. PyPI: OSBModelValidation 0.4.0, license LGPL-3.0-only. [GitHub API: created 2014-04-16, last push 2026-08-17, license LGPL-3.0]

candidates.title: HH model with OSB model validation (LEMS/NeuroML2, NEURON and GENESIS implementations)
candidates.authors: borismarin (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search LEMS test
candidates.why_relevant: Example of OMV-based CI comparing one model implemented in three simulators against shared expectations: a small cross-simulator behaviour-preservation check of the kind NeuroSem generalises. Single model, fixed tests. [GitHub API: created 2014-04-14, last push 2017-04-05, license none]

candidates.title: Collaborative infrastructure for test-driven scientific model validation
candidates.authors: Cyrus Omar, Jonathan Aldrich, Richard C. Gerkin
candidates.venue: Companion Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Software Engineering
candidates.found_via: SciUnit README links the ICSE 2014 conference paper; DOI via Crossref bibliographic query, verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Canonical citation for SciUnit, a framework for executable, data-driven model validation tests that NeuroSem may reuse. Validates models against data, not edits against a reference model.

candidates.title: NeuronUnit: A package for data-driven validation of neuron models using SciUnit
candidates.authors: Richard C. Gerkin, Justas Birgiolas, Russell J. Jarvis, Cyrus Omar, Sharon M. Crook
candidates.found_via: GitHub search neuronunit / sciunit neuron; DOI via Crossref bibliographic query, verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Citable description of NeuronUnit (GitHub scidash/neuronunit: data-driven validation of neuron and ion channel models using SciUnit). Suites of feature-level validation tests for neuron models overlap with NeuroSem feature tests; target is agreement with experimental data rather than detecting behavioural drift after transformation. GitHub repo has no detected license (API: none); last push 2021-07-18. PyPI neuronunit 0.1.8.2.

candidates.title: eFEL: electrophysiology feature extraction library
candidates.authors: Darshan Mandge, Anıl Tuncel, Aurélien Jaquier, Ilkan Kilic, Tanguy Damart, Henry Markram, et al. (8 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: DOI in README of GitHub openbraininstitute/eFEL; verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Journal citation for eFEL, the feature extractor NeuroSem plans to reuse for spike count, latency, AP shape, adaptation and related features. Feature extraction only.

candidates.title: eFEL
candidates.authors: Ranjan, Rajnish, Van Geit, Werner, Moor, Ruben, Rössert, Christian, Riquelme, Juan Luis, Damart, Tanguy (first creators per DataCite)
candidates.venue: Zenodo (software record; metadata via DataCite API)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search efel electrophysiology; CITATION.cff in BlueBrain/eFEL; DataCite API; PyPI JSON efel 5.7.34
candidates.why_relevant: eFEL software record. Concept DOI from BlueBrain/eFEL CITATION.cff; DataCite rights lgpl-3.0; newest version DOI seen 10.5281/zenodo.19604220 (version 5.7.34), matching PyPI efel 5.7.34. Development moved from BlueBrain to openbraininstitute on GitHub (GitHub license field NOASSERTION). Version and feature names must be frozen by NeuroSem.

candidates.title: HippoUnit: A software tool for the automated testing and systematic comparison of detailed models of hippocampal neurons based on electrophysiological data
candidates.authors: Sára Sáray, Christian A. Rössert, Shailesh Appukuttan, Rosanna Migliore, Paola Vitale, Carmen A. Lupascu, et al. (13 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search hippounit (KaliLab/hippounit README DOI); verified via Crossref works API; PyPI hippounit 1.4.1
candidates.why_relevant: Automated test suite that systematically compares many CA1 pyramidal cell models on multiple somatic and dendritic properties against electrophysiological data (Crossref abstract). Shares the multi-test, multi-model comparison framing; no controlled mutants, tolerance calibration, protocol selection or held-out mutation families. GitHub KaliLab/hippounit license BSD-3-Clause.

candidates.title: NetworkUnit: a SciUnit library for validation testing of spiking neural network models
candidates.authors: INM-6 (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search sciunit; PyPI JSON networkunit 0.2.2
candidates.why_relevant: SciUnit-based validation including model-to-model comparison for spiking networks (README flowchart references model-to-model). Network level rather than single-cell edits; no mutation or protocol optimisation. [GitHub API: created 2017-11-14, last push 2024-08-01, license BSD-3-Clause]

candidates.title: BluePyOpt: Leveraging Open Source Software and Cloud Infrastructure to Optimise Model Parameters in Neuroscience
candidates.authors: Werner Van Geit, Michael Gevaert, Giuseppe Chindemi, Christian Rössert, Jean-Denis Courcol, Eilif B. Muller, et al. (9 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: DOI in README of GitHub openbraininstitute/BluePyOpt; verified via Crossref works API; PyPI bluepyopt 1.14.25
candidates.why_relevant: Canonical BluePyOpt citation. Multi-protocol, feature-based fitness evaluation of neuron models (protocol plus eFEL features) is a reusable pattern for NeuroSem batteries; purpose is parameter optimisation, not regression detection. Software DOI in README: 10.5281/zenodo.19630564 (DataCite version 1.14.25).

candidates.title: BluePyEModel
candidates.authors: Mandge, Darshan, Jaquier, Aurélien, Damart, Tanguy Pierre Louis, Kilic, Ilkan, Tuncel, Anil, Arnaudon, Alexis (first creators per DataCite)
candidates.venue: Zenodo (software record; metadata via DataCite API)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search bluepyemodel; CITATION.cff; DataCite API; PyPI JSON bluepyemodel 1.0.47 and site:pypi.org WebSearch
candidates.why_relevant: Electrical model building pipeline covering feature extraction from electrophysiology, parameter optimisation and model validation on top of eFEL, BluePyEfe and BluePyOpt (PyPI description). Closest reusable source of protocol/feature battery definitions; aims at fitting and validating e-models against data, not detecting silent drift after transformations. DataCite version 1.0.47.

candidates.title: A universal workflow for creation, validation, and generalization of detailed neuronal models
candidates.authors: Maria Reva, Christian Rössert, Alexis Arnaudon, Tanguy Damart, Darshan Mandge, Anıl Tuncel, et al. (9 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: DOI in README of GitHub openbraininstitute/BluePyEModel; verified via Crossref works API (no abstract in Crossref)
candidates.why_relevant: Workflow paper for creation, validation and generalization of detailed neuronal models (title per Crossref). Generalization of validated models is conceptually adjacent to NeuroSem held-out model evaluation; content beyond title not retrieved here, so overlap depth is unverified.

candidates.title: BluePyEfe
candidates.authors: Rössert, Christian, Van Geit, Werner, Iavarone, Elisabetta, Bologna, Luca Leonardo, Damart, Tanguy, Jaquier, Aurélien (first creators per DataCite)
candidates.venue: Zenodo (software record; metadata via DataCite API)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search bluepyefe; CITATION.cff; DataCite API; PyPI bluepyefe 2.3.63
candidates.why_relevant: E-feature extraction across protocols from experimental traces (BluePyEfe). Multi-protocol feature targets; no mutation or selection. DataCite version 2.3.63.

candidates.title: IPFX: intrinsic cell features from intracellular electrophysiology data
candidates.authors: AllenInstitute (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search ipfx electrophysiology; PyPI JSON ipfx 2.1.2
candidates.why_relevant: Alternative feature extractor tied to Allen standardized current-clamp stimulus sets; relevant to NeuroSem feature/protocol definitions and to distinguishing standardized protocol batteries from optimised ones. No mutation or regression framing. [GitHub API: created 2017-12-10, last push 2026-08-14, license NOASSERTION]

candidates.title: pyelectro: analysis of electrophysiology in Python
candidates.authors: NeuralEnsemble (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search pyelectro; PyPI JSON pyelectro 0.2.7
candidates.why_relevant: NeuroML-community trace analysis library (spike detection, feature analysis) used with neurotune; alternative or complement to eFEL. [GitHub API: created 2013-08-26, last push 2026-07-24, license BSD-3-Clause]

candidates.title: Neurotune: fitting/optimization of NeuroML models
candidates.authors: NeuralEnsemble (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search neurotune; PyPI JSON neurotune 0.2.6
candidates.why_relevant: Feature-target optimisation of NeuroML models; shows existing NeuroML tooling for feature-based comparison of model outputs, without mutation-based test selection. [GitHub API: created 2012-07-16, last push 2026-07-21, license BSD-3-Clause]

candidates.title: NeuroML-DB: Sharing and characterizing data-driven neuroscience models described in NeuroML
candidates.authors: Justas Birgiolas, Vergil Haynes, Padraig Gleeson, Richard C. Gerkin, Suzanne W. Dietrich, Sharon Crook
candidates.found_via: GitHub search NeuroML-DB (scrook/neuroml-db); DOI via Crossref bibliographic query, verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: NeuroML-DB stores 1,500+ models translated to NeuroML and lets users assess stored model electrophysiology properties, with a database-scale analysis of model similarity in property/feature space (Crossref abstract). Overlaps on large-scale electrophysiological characterization of NeuroML models and on translation; does not address controlled mutations, silent drift, tolerance calibration or protocol-battery optimisation.

candidates.title: Mapping the function of neuronal ion channels in model and experiment
candidates.authors: William F Podlaski, Alexander Seeholzer, Lukas N Groschner, Gero Miesenböck, Rajnish Ranjan, Tim P Vogels
candidates.found_via: GitHub search ion channel genealogy (OpenSourceBrain/IonChannelGenealogyShowcase); DOI via Crossref bibliographic query, verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: ICGenealogy classifies 2378 NEURON ion channel models into clusters using metadata and responses to a fixed set of voltage-clamp protocols (Crossref abstract): a protocol-response fingerprint for model comparison at channel level. Partial overlap with perturbation fingerprints; no mutants, current-clamp cell-level battery, tolerance calibration or optimised selection.

candidates.title: An ion channel omnimodel for standardized biophysical neuron modelling
candidates.authors: Chaitanya Chintaluri, William Podlaski, Panos A. Bozelos, Pedro J Gonçalves, Jan-Matthis Lueckmann, Jakob H. Macke, et al. (7 authors per Crossref)
candidates.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (Channelpedia / ion channel genealogy); verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Re-expresses 3,000+ database channel models in one standard Hodgkin-Huxley form and checks that responses to voltage-clamp protocols are similar or identical (Crossref abstract). A large-scale behaviour-preservation check of a model translation, at channel level and with fixed protocols; relevant to NeuroSem valid-transformation framing.

candidates.title: Ion Channel Genealogy Visualizer (source-code similarity across ModelDB ion channel models)
candidates.authors: bozelosp (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search ion channel genealogy
candidates.why_relevant: Traces reuse and modification of channel model source files across publications via code similarity and diffs: evidence that model edits propagate, but compares code, not behaviour. [GitHub API: created 2026-09-05, last push 2026-09-05, license none]

candidates.title: Numerical Validation for Cell-Matched Neuronal Model Replay
candidates.authors: G. Blake Pierpoint, Yichen Liu (per DataCite and CITATION.cff)
candidates.venue: Zenodo software record (v0.2.1) and GitHub blakepi/neuronal-model-replay-validation
candidates.found_via: GitHub search neuron model validation; DOI badge in README; DataCite API (also surfaced by DataCite Zenodo query neuronal model replay validation)
candidates.why_relevant: Recent (repo created 2026-07-22, MIT) benchmark testing stimulus-delivery fidelity, equilibration and outcome eligibility when replaying Allen stimuli into neuron models. Its methodology doc uses solver-step refinement (0.025 down to 0.0025 ms), explicit material-change criteria on spike count, event timing and steady-state voltage, and non-evaluable outcome codes that are never converted to zero. Strong overlap with NeuroSem numerical-refinement tolerances and undefined-feature handling; no mutation operators, protocol selection or held-out mutation families. Accompanying manuscript is anonymous; no paper DOI found.

candidates.title: Loss or gain of function? Effects of ion channel mutations on neuronal firing depend on the neuron type
candidates.authors: Nils A. Koch, Lukas Sonnenberg, Ulrike B. S. Hedrich, Stephan Lauxmann, Jan Benda
candidates.found_via: GitHub search neuron model mutation / channel mutation neuron firing (nkoch1/LOFGOF2023, MIT); verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Systematically perturbs ionic current properties across a diverse set of single-compartment conductance-based models and shows firing outcomes depend on model type (Crossref abstract). Closest analogue found of a controlled biophysical perturbation family evaluated across many models; aims at channelopathy interpretation, not software regression detection or protocol selection.

candidates.title: hnn-jax: differentiable JAX reimplementation of the HNN forward model validated against an hnn_core (NEURON) test oracle
candidates.authors: m9h (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search neuron model validation
candidates.why_relevant: Treats a translated neuroscience simulator as a program under test: forward differential oracle across a Sobol-dense parameter space, finite-difference gradient oracle, and metamorphic/property oracles (zero-drive quiescence, superposition, monotonicity) in CI, per README. Overlaps NeuroSem on behaviour preservation under translation and metamorphic testing in neuroscience simulation; network/dipole level, no mutants or protocol selection. [GitHub API: created 2026-07-27, last push 2026-08-06, license MIT]

candidates.title: A Semi-Analytical Verification Framework for Pospischil-Type Cortical Neuron Models: Parameter Estimation, Independent Cross-Validation, and a Mouse-Human Comparison
candidates.authors: Vaitheeswaran Gnanaraj
candidates.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
candidates.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (cross-simulator comparison neuron models NeuroML); verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Cross-checking two independent solvers for a Pospischil-type conductance model fitted to Allen data exposed a unit error (a factor of 1000 in the voltage equation) in the numerical pipeline (Crossref abstract). Concrete example of a silent unit fault in a conductance-based model workflow, the fault class NeuroSem targets; single model, single author, not a testing framework.

candidates.title: DendroTweaks, an interactive approach for unraveling dendritic dynamics
candidates.authors: Roman Makarov, Spyridon Chavlis, Panayiota Poirazi
candidates.found_via: GitHub search neuron model validation (Poirazi-Lab/DendroTweaks, MPL-2.0); DOI in README verified via Crossref works API; PyPI dendrotweaks 0.5.2
candidates.why_relevant: Toolbox for creating and validating single-cell biophysical models with active dendrites (GitHub/PyPI description). Adjacent model-validation tooling; not transformation testing.

candidates.title: NeuroForgeAI: toolkit for building optimized biophysical neuron models from recordings
candidates.authors: rhkrohan (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search neuron model validation
candidates.why_relevant: README describes cross-validation on independent stimulus protocols, local perturbation sensitivity analysis, robustness testing, and advanced stimulation tests (ramps, bursts, noise). Combines multi-protocol validation with parameter perturbation in a fitting workflow; small unlicensed student-scale repo, no mutation testing or protocol selection. [GitHub API: created 2025-06-30, last push 2025-06-30, license none]

candidates.title: PyNNShowcase: testing interactions/conversions between NeuroML and PyNN
candidates.authors: OpenSourceBrain (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search org:OpenSourceBrain test
candidates.why_relevant: Community repository for testing model conversions between NeuroML and PyNN simulators; conversion-equivalence testing is part of NeuroSem valid-transformation scope. [GitHub API: created 2016-03-16, last push 2026-08-17, license none]

candidates.title: AllenInstituteNeuroML: testing interaction between Allen Institute models and NeuroML
candidates.authors: OpenSourceBrain (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search org:OpenSourceBrain test
candidates.why_relevant: Converted Allen cell models in NeuroML with tests; a potential source of reference models with standardized-stimulus provenance and an example of conversion checking. [GitHub API: created 2014-08-26, last push 2026-05-19, license NOASSERTION]

candidates.title: mod2neuroml: pipelines for generating NeuroML2/LEMS from NEURON mod files
candidates.authors: NeuroML (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search org:NeuroML NeuroML2
candidates.why_relevant: Automated NMODL-to-NeuroML translation: a transformation type whose semantic preservation NeuroSem could test. [GitHub API: created 2017-08-30, last push 2017-08-30, license none]

candidates.title: mod2nml: NMODL to NeuroML language translator
candidates.authors: ninadakolekar (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search topic:neuroml
candidates.why_relevant: Another NMODL-to-NeuroML translator (archived repo); same relevance as mod2neuroml. [GitHub API: created 2018-11-05, last push 2019-10-03, license none]

candidates.title: Neuro-Klea: Knowledge vaLidated Expert AI assistant for neuroscience
candidates.authors: NeuroML (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search org:NeuroML validation
candidates.why_relevant: AI assistant from the NeuroML organisation with a general-purpose agent with coding capabilities, RAG, and an MCP server for NeuroML (README). Evidence that AI-assisted NeuroML model editing is emerging, relevant to NeuroSem AI-transformation case study; no behavioural drift testing described in README. [GitHub API: created 2025-08-07, last push 2026-09-11, license GPL-3.0]

candidates.title: MitralSuite: validation of olfactory bulb mitral cell models with NeuroElectro data using NeuronUnit
candidates.authors: JustasB (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search neuronunit
candidates.why_relevant: Applied NeuronUnit suite comparing multiple published cell models on electrophysiological properties; data-validation, not transformation testing. [GitHub API: created 2016-05-20, last push 2016-07-03, license MIT]

candidates.title: netpyneunit: SciUnit tests for NetPyNE models
candidates.authors: lakesare (GitHub owner; individual authors not verified)
candidates.found_via: GitHub search sciunit
candidates.why_relevant: SciUnit test integration for NetPyNE models; shows executable model-test tooling beyond NeuroML. [GitHub API: created 2021-06-04, last push 2022-05-12, license MIT]

candidates.title: EDEN: A High-Performance, General-Purpose, NeuroML-Based Neural Simulator
candidates.authors: Sotirios Panagiotou, Harry Sidiropoulos, Dimitrios Soudris, Mario Negrello, Christos Strydis
candidates.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (cross-simulator comparison neuron models NeuroML); verified via Crossref works API; PyPI eden-simulator seen in site:pypi.org WebSearch
candidates.why_relevant: EDEN is a NeuroML-based simulator; OSB EDENShowcase (GitHub) tests it with NeuroML models. Candidate for optional cross-simulator transformations; infrastructure only.

candidates.title: Usability and functionality of NeuroML description language evaluated using three distinct spiking neuron models
candidates.authors: Lehtimäki Mikko, Linne Marja-Leena
candidates.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (reproducibility neuron model conversion NEURON NeuroML); verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Conference abstract evaluating NeuroML usability using three spiking neuron models (title per Crossref); likely touches reimplementation fidelity, content not retrieved, overlap unverified.

candidates.title: Improving the Efficacy of Testing Scientific Software: Insights from Mutation Testing
candidates.authors: Kris Roker, Upulee Kanewala
candidates.venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW)
candidates.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (mutation testing scientific simulation software); verified via Crossref works API (no abstract)
candidates.why_relevant: Mutation testing applied to scientific software (IEEE ICST workshops 2024). Generic prior art that NeuroSem must not claim: mutation testing of scientific code; not neuron-model semantics or protocol batteries.

candidates.why_relevant: Metamorphic testing of scientific software; generic prior art for metamorphic testing claims.

candidates.authors: Upulee Kanewala, James M. Bieman, Asa Ben‐Hur
candidates.found_via: Crossref bibliographic query (metamorphic testing scientific simulation software); verified via Crossref works API
candidates.why_relevant: Predicting metamorphic relations for scientific software; generic prior art on test-oracle construction for scientific code.
